A1.justification: Both PDFs describe REVERSE, with matching authors, method, training dataset and retained experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations, threshold and temperature analyses, and qualitative results in Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds Qwen2.5-VL evaluations and an analysis of backtracking behavior in Section 4 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same special tokens, masked training objective, hierarchical backtracking, rejection sampling and query rewriting. Qwen2.5-VL implements the existing framework with a different training recipe; no new proposed algorithm component is introduced.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same LLaVA-derived training sources and CHAIR-MSCOCO, AMBER-G/D, MMHal, HaloQuest, POPE and MME-Hall evaluations. Qwen training uses subsets of existing data. Discriminative evaluations move to the appendix rather than being removed.

E2.justification: v2 adds a fine-tuned Qwen2.5-VL control and a corresponding DoLA comparison in Tables 1–3 and A.1. Comparator membership in the retained LLaVA experiments is unchanged; no new hallucination-mitigation baseline algorithm is introduced.

E3.justification: v2 adds a distinct Qwen2.5-VL 3B experimental regime: full fine-tuning with matched 100k training subsets and a generative threshold of 0.01, alongside the retained LLaVA LoRA experiments. It also introduces a diagnostic evaluation of 1,004 AMBER-G samples. Existing benchmark metrics, evaluators and LLaVA decoding settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.2 adds a focused analysis of verification triggers, skipped outputs, harmful corrections and regeneration rounds on 1,004 AMBER-G examples. Existing component ablations, threshold tradeoffs, temperature sensitivity and qualitative examples are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report 100-round bootstrapping and 95% confidence intervals. v2 applies the same reporting practice to Qwen results; the retained LLaVA intervals are unchanged, and no new seed, repeated-run or statistical-testing procedure is specified.

E6.justification: v2 adds Qwen results across all retained benchmarks, including REVERSE scores of 45.1% on HaloQuest and 3.15 with a 0.29 hallucination rate on MMHal, plus new backtracking findings. Existing LLaVA numerical results are unchanged. The new Qwen AMBER-D baseline conflicts between Table A.1 (87.7) and Table A.4 (85.0), leaving that particular comparison unresolved.

T1.justification: The masked likelihood objective and appendix metric definitions remain mathematically unchanged. Equation renumbering, moving the conditional probability expression inline, and clarifying target masking introduce no new derivation, assumption or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion increase the headline HaloQuest improvement claim from 28% to 34%, reflecting the added Qwen comparison. The central contributions—a unified self-verification framework and the 1.3M-sample dataset—remain unchanged.

C2.justification: New Appendix C substantially expands applicability qualifications through discussion of missing dataset edge cases, GPT-generated augmentation bias and biases inherited from source datasets. v2 also adds interpretations of verification efficiency, model-specific confidence calibration and DoLA's weaker transfer to Qwen, while retaining the existing expressiveness and discriminative-task limitations.

D1.justification: Appendix F adds exact LLaVA backbone and freezing details and the Qwen training recipe, including learning rate, hardware and training time. It specifies a global batch of 128 where v1 stated 16 without its scope, so an actual LLaVA batch change is not established. Appendix A additionally announces Qwen checkpoints and their upstream licensing dependency.

R1.justification: v2 adds references concerning newer VLMs, explicit uncertainty, calibration, efficient backtracking and dataset bias. The central positioning relative to Woodpecker and LURE remains intact, although Figure 5 newly calls REVERSE the first controllable VLM supporting the illustrated hallucination–coverage tradeoff.

P1.justification: v2 selectively rewrites experimental descriptions and discussion, reorders discussion topics, and moves discriminative-task discussion into Appendix E. The appendix gains a limitations section, while the introduction and method narrative remain largely intact.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to predominantly single-column layout. Figure 1 is rearranged horizontally; the HaloQuest and MMHal tables are reorganized side by side; discriminative results move to the appendix; and tables expand for Qwen. The negative-generation prompt is redesigned, while existing plots and qualitative examples retain their content.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens evidence of transfer beyond LLaVA through the matched-data Qwen experiments and provides useful dataset limitations, backtracking diagnostics and training details. These are meaningful but limited gains: the new minimal-overhead claim lacks timing measurements, and Tables A.1 and A.4 disagree on the Qwen AMBER-D baseline. The original experimental findings remain unchanged.
